title: Apple Health export (raw)
description: The subset of an `apple_health_export/export.xml` that packages/connectors/src/providers/apple-health reads, after parseExport.js has turned tags into objects. Names are Apple's, not ours. Everything is optional: a real export is mostly holes, and the holes are the point. Measured over one real export — 379,700 <Record> tags and 30 <Workout> tags spanning 2017-11-23 to 2026-07-25, 29 distinct record types, of which this connector reads 4. Coverage of what we read: stepCount 44,745 records across 2,708 days; restingHeartRate 115 records across 115 days; sleepAnalysis 21 records across 2 days; heartRateVariabilitySDNN 19 records across 7 days. Recovery signals are that sparse in a real export, and a caller sees it as recovery.missing rather than as invented numbers. Read `sourceName` before reading anything into that sparsity: see the note on it below.

records.description: Attributes lifted off each opening <Record> tag. Nested <MetadataEntry> children carry nothing this connector needs.

type.description: HealthKit identifier. Only four are read: HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRateVariabilitySDNN, HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRestingHeartRate, HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount, HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis. The other 25 types in the export — walking asymmetry, headphone audio exposure, basal energy — are read by nobody and are not part of this contract.

value.description: Numeric as a string for quantity types; a HKCategoryValue* name for category types. Over the measured export no read record had a missing, non-numeric, zero, or negative value — unlike Garmin, Apple does not write not-measured sentinels into <Record>. Absence is expressed by the record simply not existing.

unit.description: ms for SDNN, count/min for resting heart rate, count for steps. Absent on category records such as sleep, which have no unit.

startDate.description: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS ±HHMM", e.g. "2026-07-20 08:30:00 +0800". appleDateToIso converts it to ISO 8601. All 379,702 records in the measured export matched this format with no exceptions, and all carried one single offset (+0800) — a export that crossed time zones would carry several, which the format handles and nothing downstream assumes away.

endDate.description: Same format. Used as the fallback when startDate is absent, and as the night key for sleep — a sleep interval belongs to the day it ends on.

sourceName.description: The device or app that wrote the record, and the only field that says where a signal actually came from. Apple Health is a destination as much as a source: a watch writes to it, and so does every app that syncs into it. **A signal being present in an Apple Health export does not mean an Apple Watch measured it.** In the measured export, `Connect` — Garmin Connect syncing in — begins on 2025-11-12 and accounts for all 21 sleep records and 109 of 115 resting heart rates, while the only 19 HRV records come from an Apple Watch that stopped writing on 2023-08-03. So the same file holds two device eras two years apart, and Garmin's sync carries no HRV at all. A caller told only that "Apple Health has HRV" would believe a signal is available that this user has not produced since 2023. Also load-bearing for steps: 6 distinct writers, and 109 of 2,708 step days (4.0%) had two or more, so the connector takes the largest per-recorder sum rather than summing them.

workouts.description: Attributes off each opening <Workout> tag, plus the nested <WorkoutStatistics> children collected under `statistics`. Reading only the opening tag is not enough in this dialect — see `statistics`.

workoutActivityType.description: HKWorkoutActivityType* name. The measured export contains Running, Walking, Hiking and Cycling. Types absent from the connector's map fall back to "recovery", which would be wrong for a hard session — HKWorkoutActivityTypeMixedCardio and HKWorkoutActivityTypeHighIntensityIntervalTraining land there today. Recorded as a known limitation: the honest mapping needs a workout type the domain does not have, so it is written down rather than guessed.

duration.description: Numeric as a string. Present on 100% of workouts in the measured export.

durationUnit.description: "min" on every workout measured. The connector reads `duration` as minutes; an export carrying another unit would need converting rather than trusting.

totalEnergyBurned.description: Active energy in kilocalories, in the older dialect that put it on the tag. Present on 0.0% of workouts in the measured export — see `statistics`. Still read first when present, so both dialects work.

totalDistance.description: Distance in km, older dialect. Also 0.0% in the measured export.

sourceName.description: The app or device that wrote the workout. Present on 100% of workouts measured, and worth keeping: which writer produced a session explains whether it carries energy at all.

statistics.description: Nested <WorkoutStatistics> elements, keyed by their `type`. This is where a current Apple export puts a workout's energy and distance, and a parser that read only the opening tag reported every session as having no load. Coverage over the measured export: ActiveEnergyBurned and a Distance* statistic on all 30 workouts (100%), whether written by the watch directly or synced in from Garmin Connect.

sum.description: Total over the workout, for additive quantities such as energy and distance. **`0` is a not-measured sentinel, not zero calories.** Every workout written by a watch or synced from Garmin Connect in the measured export carries a real total, so the rate here is 0% — but a third-party gym app writing into HealthKit in that same export produced sum="0" on session after session. Any app can write a workout, and one that measures no energy still writes the statistic. Reported as no load, which is what it is.

average.description: Present on averaged quantities such as heart rate. Not read today.

unit.description: "Cal" for energy — HealthKit's spelling of kilocalories — and "km" for distance, on every statistic measured. A statistic in any other unit is left alone rather than converted on a guess.
